entityDescription:
The SEI Incubator was established in 2020 in Avellino as an innovation hub in Italy's rural areas. SEI was born thanks to a group of young professionals and entrepreneurs who shared the goal of revitalizing rural regions by nurturing entrepreneurial ideas, with a focus on sustainability, ethics, and innovation. SEI provides support and training to all young entrepreneurs that want to create a startup, offering them a physical space to work on their ideas independently and without constraints. SEI also offers consulting and training services to SMEs, assisting them in bringing innovation to their ecosystem through open innovation pathways.

Today, SEI has opened a new hub in Benevento and is planning to open additional spaces in other parts of Italy. The SEI Incubator has supported over 50 startups and entrepreneurial teams, investing a total of 64,500 euros in 5 companies. They regularly engage in incubation, acceleration, training, and networking activities and have established partnerships with universities, research centers, SMEs, and industry associations.In late 2020, SEI launched its first call for ideas, "Demetra," for startups, receiving over 54 applications from all over Italy. In three years of operation, SEI has developed an innovative, strategic, and scalable model with the aim of expanding nationally, providing vitality to entrepreneurship in rural areas by replicating the model established in Avellino.In late 2022, SEI launched its second call for ideas, "Traiano," in Benevento, which received more than 30 applications. Their support for startups includes incubation, go-to-market strategies, and fundraising.SEI has organized and managed two hackathons, over 20 specific webinars, and two innovation programs with local SMEs. They host often Demo Days for their startups with investors and actively participate in most startup events and industry fairs.

entityDescription:
AeroPhoto Co Ltd, founded in 2014 and based in Thessaloniki, Greece, is an aerial survey and geospatial data processing company with expertise in acquisition, analysis, mapping and delivery of geospatial information. It is committed to airborne spatial data acquisition of the earth’s surface and its advanced processing, leading to value-added geo-information products. With our long experience and reliability, we provide high quality and accurate topographic and geospatial raw data and derivatives, such as aerial photography and LiDAR data, using state-of-the-art cutting-edge technologies, cameras and sensors. The company successfully operates missions in Greece, across European Union and in Middle East territories. 

Customer-focused and committed to innovation, our products and services are constantly evolving to meet the needs of a broad range of market sectors e.g. forestry, land administration, transportation and infrastructure, archaeology, natural disaster management, pipelines, and requirements of the most complex projects. AeroPhoto Co Ltd undertakes aerial photography, LiDAR, thermal and hyperspectral survey missions operating the most up to date and advanced aerial survey equipment, and as such is in the position of being able to provide customers with high quality, unique and cost-effective solutions. In collaboration with private and public sector, universities and institutes we participate in research programs whose prerequisite is ultra-high resolution aerial images or LiDAR datasets.

Flight missions for the acquisition of ultra-high-resolution aerial imagery and LiDAR data, are carried out by specially modified, EASA certified aircrafts. Aircrafts are equipped with a wide range of airborne mapping systems, digital large and medium format aerial cameras (e.g. Vexcel Ultracam Eagle Μ3, Phase One iXU-RS 1000), LiDAR sensors (e.g. Riegl LMS VQ-1560ii, VQ-880-G II), hyperspectral and thermal cameras (e.g. CASI & TABI), accurate GPS/IMU systems and other scientific equipment. Our sensors and aircrafts allow us to execute capture with a GSD range of 1.5 to 50cm.

The Laboratory of Spectroscopy is one of the largest laboratories at the ISSP UL and it combines a variety of research methods related to optical, magnetic and electron spectroscopy.
The range of materials includes both bulk and polycrystals, glass, thin films, nanomaterials, liquids and gases. The available infrastructure includes both standard measurements (absorption, excitation, steady-state and time-resolved luminescence spectra) over a wide temperature range (6 K to 700 K) as well as vibrational (Raman and Fourier infrared) spectroscopy, ellipsometry, electron paramagnetic resonance , optically detectable magnetic resonance, subnanosecond luminescence characterization, thermostimulated luminescence measurement, ablation spectroscopy and X - ray photoelectron spectroscopy equipment.
The staff of the laboratory has extensive experience in the spectroscopic characterization of solid state materials and actively provides services to academic and industrial partners.

We have a long track record of processing (https://cryotempo-eolis.org/) and disseminating (https://cs2eo.org/) CryoSat-2 data for ESA, as well as having overseen the Digital Twin Earth - Antarctica Project. We would like to take the lead on ingesting, processing and disseminating CryoSat-2 within a proposed HIGHWAY consortium. CryoSat-2 has been named as a priority Earth Explorer mission within the ITT text, and Earth Explorer missions generally have higher risk, lower commonality processes than other data sources. We believe this justifies the inclusion of specialist consortium partners to handle them. 
Further, our experience with CryoSat-2’s geospatial point cloud data will be valuable when dealing with other, similar data sets such as those of Sentinel-3. Drawing on our successful cs2eo.org service and our currently in-development service Specklia (https://pypi.org/project/specklia/), we can offer innovative, advanced data access techniques for geospatial point cloud data to a consortium, allowing it to pull ahead of competing consortia who might be overly focussed on raster data. Lastly, we are recognised by ESA as proven experts on the conversion of CryoSat-2’s geospatial point clouds to a raster form (the CryoTEMPO-EOLIS Gridded Product – an operational product for ESA).

The identification, assessment, further development and commercialisation of technologies and knowledge is our core business. We offer our services to leading public research organisations, innovation and start-up creation networks and internationally oriented companies, both corporates and SMEs.
In the field of public research, Atrineo AG is working for all four major research organisations (Max Planck Society, Fraunhofer Society, Helmholtz Association, Leibniz Association) as well as for leading universities in Spain and Europe.
Typical projects of Atrineo AG are the further development of activities in the field of knowledge and technology transfer, i.e. the design, establishment and optimisation of structures, systems and processes as well as the support and consultancy service for singular transfer cases.
